findings.problem: Draft AC11 says 'retains only real completed runs/transcripts, including partial failures'. Completed can be read as excluding failed/interrupted-arm audit data, contrary to the source contract.
findings.impact: A test/implementation could discard actual failed-arm diagnostics while claiming AC11 compliance. This is wording ambiguity, not a demonstrated runtime defect.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'retains actual runs/transcripts including failed/interrupted-arm audit data; only durably completed seeds are reusable'. Preserve empty runs for pre-run no-task/underpowered/gold-leak.
findings.evidence: acceptance-criteria.md AC11 quoted above; operator-decisions.md requires actual runs/transcripts on partial failure; specification.md:222 explicitly preserves actual partial-failure runs, :338 classifies failed/unrecoverable running seeds as run-failed. Lifecycle distinguishes audit retention from completed-seed reuse.

limitations: Project validator implements a Draft-2020-12 subset, not full external metaschema conformance; positive/negative samples do not prove all inputs.
Synthetic schema checks do not establish runtime arithmetic, verdict precedence, crash recovery, lock ordering, confidence dedup, spend accounting or live measurements.
Late-drift check only compares JSON serialization of a synthetic envelope, not persistence or on-disk comparison immutability. Duplicate-ID assertion checks Set detection, not runtime loader refusal.

Path samples do not prove symlink containment or gold base-ref existence/removal. Cleanup/signals, identical arms, stdout isolation, terminal confirmation and dry-run zero writes remain runtime test obligations.
Global docs index/roadmap follow-ups are outside ownership; global index completeness is not certified.
No new unresolved owner policy decision discovered. Existing operator decisions not reopened. Orchestrator owns minor AC clarification; freeze/runtime dispatch remain gated.
